entries.title: Endpoint transport reads prompt, signal, timeoutMs, and timeout_s from ExecutePromptOptions
entries.summary: The endpoint transport's executePrompt method processes only five fields from ExecutePromptOptions: prompt (required), signal (AbortSignal), timeoutMs (milliseconds), timeout_s (seconds), and silently ignores all others including agent, max_total_s, max_turns, member_id, member_name, model, resume, session_id, and substitutions.

entries.title: Provider abstraction: six adapters, never assume Claude
entries.summary: src/providers/index.ts registers exactly six LlmProvider adapters -- claude, codex, copilot, agy, opencode, none -- matching the LlmProvider union at src/types.ts:4. There is no gemini adapter. Any auth, credential or dispatch change must route through the ProviderAdapter interface rather than assuming Claude-specific fields, and getProvider() defaults to claude only when the argument is null/undefined.

entries.title: Same-slug callers now open two SqliteProvider handles on one kb.sqlite
entries.summary: Keying the KB provider cache by (slug, repoPath) means two local clones of the same remote get two separate SqliteProvider instances pointed at the same kb.sqlite file; this is safe by design because init sets WAL plus busy_timeout=5000.

entries.title: The endpoint transport now honors timeoutMs and timeout_s, with a 120s default deadline
entries.summary: Supersedes the earlier claim that executePrompt reads only prompt and signal: both shape adapters now resolve a request deadline from options.timeoutMs, options.timeout_s, config.timeoutMs or DEFAULT_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS (120s), so an unconfigured endpoint dispatch is always bounded.

entries.title: KB provider cache is now keyed by (slug, repoPath), not slug alone
entries.summary: getKbProviders/_providers Map keys on providerKey(slug, repoPath) via a NUL join, so two callers resolving to the same project slug but different repoPath values get distinct provider instances, each anchored at its own caller's repoPath.

entries.title: {{secure.NAME}} values arrive already shell-escaped, and the escaping is OS-branched
entries.summary: execute_command replaces each {{secure.NAME}} token with a value that has ALREADY been quoted for the target member's shell -- escapePowerShellArg for windows members, escapeShellArg otherwise, chosen from agentOs. Reference the token bare in a command string; wrapping it in your own quotes double-escapes the value and surfaces as a false 401 or invalid-token error.

entries.title: bd prints literal JSON null, not [], for an empty dolt remote list
entries.summary: `bd dolt remote list --json` emits the JSON literal null when no Dolt remotes are configured. parseDoltRemoteList maps that to [] before its non-array guard, so an unwired repo reads as "no remotes" rather than a parse error; every other non-array shape still throws. Without the null branch, checkDoltRemoteAbsent returns ok:false ("could not parse") for a repo that is simply not wired to a Dolt remote.

entries.title: Local members use host OAuth; provision_llm_auth skips them
entries.summary: Local fleet members share the orchestrator's own machine, so they use whatever OAuth session is already active on that host. provision_llm_auth explicitly skips local members rather than attempting to provision credentials for them.

entries.title: sprint-logs/ must never carry a blanket directory ignore -- .gitignore says so inline
entries.summary: A directory-level rule such as '/sprint-logs/' shadows everything beneath it, un-ignore patterns included, and silently breaks the sprint cost ledger because auto-sprint.js stages it with an unguarded `git add sprint-logs/`. Merged main keeps only scoped rules and records the prohibition as a comment in .gitignore itself, so the lesson survives without depending on the KB.

entries.title: kb-setup is the one kb tool that takes repo_path but resolves no KB
entries.summary: Fifteen of the sixteen src/tools/kb-*.ts tools spread kbScopeFields and forward repo_remote_url to getKbProviders; kb-setup is excluded by design because its repo_path only locates a .git dir for hook installation and it writes a single global config, never selecting a project KB.

entries.title: A fallback message sharing the assertion's alternate keyword makes a test vacuous
entries.summary: checkDoltRemoteAbsent's bd-unavailable fallback messages all contain the word "unavailable", so the old combined assertion /Dolt-level remotes|unavailable/ was satisfied on any machine without bd without ever reaching the parser under test. Merged main closes this by probing bd --version first and asserting the two cases separately. The reusable trap: never OR an assertion's success keyword with its own fallback keyword.

entries.title: hasOppositePolarity matches on word-boundary regexes, not substrings
entries.summary: audn.ts hasOppositePolarity tests NEGATIVE_PATTERNS/POSITIVE_PATTERNS with precompiled word-boundary regexes, so "prefixed" no longer collides with "fixed".

entries.title: apra-fleet-se's plain npm test never sets APRA_FLEET_TEST_CONCURRENCY
entries.summary: packages/apra-fleet-se's "test" script runs node --test directly with --test-concurrency=8, but does NOT set the APRA_FLEET_TEST_CONCURRENCY env var -- only the separate test:unit/test:integration/test:record scripts (which route through scripts/run-tests.mjs) set it. A scaledTimeout()/waitFor() call that relies on the env var being set will silently use an unscaled timeout under plain npm test.

entries.title: The endpoint transport's memberless pricing does resolve real cost through the engine's tier path
entries.summary: Despite the transport sending one configured model for every tier, an endpoint dispatch made with model:'premium' (or cheap/standard) and config.pricing set is priced by _resolveCost() as REAL pricing, incrementing budget._pricedReal -- the tier keyword still gates entry into the real-pricing branch.

entries.title: The .trim() guard in resolveProjectSlug is provably redundant and cannot be pinned by any test
entries.summary: project-slug.ts guards its remote-URL short-circuit twice, but the outer remoteUrl.trim() check is unreachable-by-effect given slugify, so no input can distinguish its removal and no regression test can pin it.

entries.title: endpoint/core.mjs is unreachable from outside apra-fleet-client -- package.json has no ./endpoint subpath
entries.summary: packages/apra-fleet-client declares an "exports" map, so the new endpoint transport core can only be imported by siblings inside the package via a relative path; any external import fails with ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED.

entries.title: agent()/command() now emit activity:end for a WorkflowError raised directly by fleetApi, not just ones the engine itself throws
entries.summary: The catch blocks in _agentDispatch()/_commandDispatch() used to assume every instanceof WorkflowError had already had activity:end emitted at an internal throw site; that broke for a FleetApi (like the endpoint transport) that raises the engine's own typed errors directly from executePrompt/executeCommand.

entries.title: dist/ is fully gitignored -- the dist-pm staleness guard is a local-only, no-op-on-CI check
entries.summary: packages/apra-fleet-se/test/contracts-schema-dist-staleness-guard.test.mjs only activates when a developer's local dist/agents/schemas build artifact exists; dist/ has never been tracked in git (repo-root .gitignore line 2: `dist/`). Fixing a reported staleness failure means running `npm run dist-pm` locally, not committing anything -- there is nothing under dist/ to commit.

entries.title: The engine's typed error taxonomy now lives in apra-fleet-client, not apra-fleet-workflow
entries.summary: WorkflowError and its subclasses moved to packages/apra-fleet-client/src/errors/workflow-errors.mjs ('@apralabs/apra-fleet-client/errors'); packages/apra-fleet-workflow/src/workflow/errors.mjs is now a re-export shim. The move was forced by the dependency direction: apra-fleet-workflow depends on apra-fleet-client, so any transport living in the client package could otherwise only reach the taxonomy through a circular package dependency.

entries.title: Root npm test does not run the client or workflow package suites
entries.summary: scripts/run-all-tests.mjs drives only vitest and the apra-fleet-se workspace, and vitest's include glob misses packages/*/test/*.test.mjs on both the directory name and the extension, so a green root run proves nothing about the endpoint transport.

entries.title: Member OS resolution: always via agent.os
entries.summary: The orchestrator and each fleet member can independently run Windows/Mac/Linux -- local members share the orchestrator's own OS, but remote members can be any OS regardless of the orchestrator's. Never assume a target member's shell/OS matches the orchestrator's.

entries.title: FleetWorkflow.agent() requires member_name or member_id even for a memberless FleetApi
entries.summary: agent() hard-throws before dispatch when neither member_name nor member_id is set, so an endpoint-transport caller must still pass a placeholder member identifier despite there being no member behind the transport.

entries.title: Assert details.reason to prove a typed error passed through the engine unwrapped
entries.summary: FleetWorkflow's agent() catch re-throws an instanceof WorkflowError untouched but wraps anything else in a fresh FleetTransportError, so an instanceof-only assertion cannot tell pass-through from re-wrap and silently passes under a regression.

entries.title: Local vs remote member dispatch paths
entries.summary: Local members share the orchestrator's own machine and credentials, so no SSH or file probe is needed -- check agent.agentType === 'local' and short-circuit. Remote members require actual SSH connectivity and credential probes.

entries.title: Four resolveRepoPath helpers exist in src/tools, but only prime and stats ever had the null-to-cwd shape
entries.summary: kb-session-prime.ts and kb-stats.ts returned string|null and degraded to process.cwd(); kb-export.ts and kb-import.ts have always returned string and thrown, so they were never part of the b4g.7 anchor defect despite the bead naming kb-export as a third instance.

entries.title: gitRepos is an access list; only a single URL-shaped entry is a usable origin
entries.summary: agent.gitRepos is declared string[] and holds bare "Owner/Repo" access identifiers, not clone URLs. knownRepoRemoteUrl (now in src/services/member-remote-url.ts, re-exported from execute-prompt.ts) returns a URL only when gitRepos has EXACTLY one entry AND that entry is scheme-qualified; anything else yields undefined rather than a guessed URL.

entries.title: An endpoint-transport test stub must reject on abort, not merely never resolve
entries.summary: A fetch stub that returns a forever-pending promise hangs any endpoint-transport test that expects a cancellation, because postJson only classifies an abort inside its catch blocks -- the stub must reject with an AbortError when its signal fires, the way a real fetch does.

entries.title: Lockfile drift is invisible to npm test
entries.summary: A PR review that runs only 'npm test' cannot catch package.json/package-lock.json drift (e.g. a dependency override added to package.json without regenerating the lockfile), because npm test runs against whatever node_modules is already populated. Only 'npm ci' -- the reproducible-install path CI actually uses -- reproduces that failure.

entries.title: registerAllTools can be driven by a 4-line fake McpServer, unlocking every handler body for testing
entries.summary: The 'no test loads tool-registry.ts' gap is structural but trivially closable: a fake with tool()/server.sendLoggingMessage() records every registered handler and runs in ~2s.

entries.title: postJson now distinguishes an aborted fetch (CancelledError) from a genuine network failure (FleetTransportError)
entries.summary: postJson in http.mjs used to classify every fetch rejection as kind:'network', which always yields FleetTransportError and made cooperative requestStop() cancellation indistinguishable from a real socket failure at the engine boundary.

entries.title: normalizeUsage drops a provider report that carries only total_tokens
entries.summary: The endpoint core treats usage as unreported unless the provider broke out an input or output count; a body with total_tokens alone yields null, so the whole usage key is omitted and the call records as unknown spend.

entries.title: resolveProjectSlug prefers an explicit git remote URL over shelling git against repo_path
entries.summary: resolveProjectSlug(cwd, remoteUrl) slugifies remoteUrl directly when supplied and only falls back to `git remote get-url origin` against cwd, then the repo dirname, then 'default', when no URL is given -- letting remote members (whose repo_path is unreachable from the fleet server host) resolve to the same slug as a local clone.

entries.title: Repo-root npm test does not run the workspace node:test suites -- only CI does
entries.summary: scripts/run-all-tests.mjs runs vitest plus apra-fleet-se only, so a green root npm test says nothing about apra-fleet-client or apra-fleet-workflow; ci.yml closes the gap with a separate npm test --workspaces step.

entries.title: Endpoint adapters must derive HTTP ok from status, not from response.ok
entries.summary: postJson in src/endpoint/http.mjs computes ok as status 200-299 and always consumes the body once, so hand-written fetch stubs only need {status, text()} and both the success and failure paths see the same already-read body.

entries.title: SqliteProvider freshness verdicts must be suppressed, not re-hashed, when the repo anchor is unreachable
entries.summary: A repo_path that does not exist on this host (the remote-member case) must never fall back to process.cwd() as the freshness anchor, and must not be re-hashed against it either -- both checkFreshness and freshnessSweep now short-circuit to a no-op verdict via a shared anchorIsMissing() check instead.

entries.title: kb_session_prime must pass an explicit repo_path to getKbProviders verbatim, never through resolveRepoPath
entries.summary: Validating repo_path before handing it to getKbProviders converts a remote member's unreachable path into the fleet server's own cwd, silently staling healthy entries in the shared project KB; the anchor must stay honestly missing.

entries.title: agent() returns structuredContent.response verbatim when no schema is given
entries.summary: For a no-schema dispatch the engine returns structured.response unmodified whenever the transport supplies it, so the endpoint transport's reply text reaches a workflow script byte-for-byte; only the wrapper-stripping fallback path (older MCP servers with no structuredContent.response) rewrites the text.

entries.title: postJson classifies by signal state at all three call sites, including the body-read catch
entries.summary: A cancellation or deadline expiry can surface as a response.text() rejection rather than a fetch rejection, so postJson checks the signal's own aborted state at the body-read catch too, via a shared classifyBySignalState() helper.

entries.title: Memberless getMemberModelPricing signals unpriced with an error key and no pricing key
entries.summary: The engine's _getMemberPricing treats a parsed payload as unpriced when parsed.error is truthy OR parsed.pricing is missing, degrading to null and warning once per member; it never throws, so an endpoint transport must use that channel rather than rejecting.

entries.title: Do not use AbortSignal.timeout() for a request deadline in this repo -- its timer is unref'd
entries.summary: AbortSignal.timeout()'s internal timer does not keep the Node event loop alive, so a deadline built on it can be silently skipped when the only other pending work is a fetch with no live handle yet.

entries.title: Wrap getKbProviders with a delegating vi.mock to assert real provider anchoring
entries.summary: To assert which dbPath/repoPath a kb tool actually anchored at, vi.mock kb-providers.js with importOriginal, spread the actual module and replace only getKbProviders with a spy that delegates to the real one and records (cwd, remoteUrl, providers).

entries.title: The endpoint transport sends one configured model, so tier keywords never resolve
entries.summary: Both endpoint shape adapters send config.model on every dispatch and ignore the engine's per-dispatch cheap/standard/premium tier keyword, because there is no member to resolve a tier against; the memberless pricing method therefore reports the same configured-model price for all three tiers rather than a per-tier table.

entries.title: A missing-anchor freshness regression surfaces first as kb_list dropping entries, not as a stale-flag assertion
entries.summary: In tests/knowledge/kb-remote-member-e2e.test.ts the four remote-member assertions live in one it(), so removing SqliteProvider's anchorIsMissing guard fails at the SAME DATABASE read-back (line 165) and never reaches the raw stale-row check (line 181).

entries.title: Engine envelope contract: structuredContent.usage must be omitted, never zero-filled
entries.summary: FleetWorkflow decides an activity had real spend with `typeof reportedUsage.total_tokens === 'number'`, and prices it from usage.input_tokens/usage.output_tokens. A transport that zero-fills usage when the provider reported none makes a paid call read as real-but-free spend; the field must be absent instead. execute_prompt itself emits it with a conditional spread for exactly this reason.

entries.title: One anchor policy, three branches: verbatim for read tools, hard-fail for kb_export
entries.summary: kb_session_prime and kb_stats pass a supplied repo_path to getKbProviders verbatim so an unreachable remote anchor stays honestly missing; kb_export deliberately keeps throwing instead, because it writes into repo_path -- and it throws before getKbProviders, so it never anchors at the server cwd either.
